images.name: The covenant as a cord tied, thickened, and held at the other end
images.source: chain map: 4. Covenant Gives Intimacy Its Form / Subchannel A. The Relation as Knot and Obligation; chain map: S13. An Oath Is Sworn, Thickened, and Released
images.scene: Two parties tie a cord between them. The knot is pulled tight and the cord is thickened until it cannot be slipped. The other party holds its end. What is lawful is what has been untied; what is forbidden stays knotted.

members.role: the cord or fetter that binds
the cord grown thick after being thin
the women's grip on their end of the cord
untying: what is not untied for you
the knot loosened for what lies beyond
binding one thing to another; the decree fastened upon you
the marriage contract as the knot
the right hands that tie the knot
the oath sworn by the right hand

images.containment: The women took from you a firm covenant, and the word lets it be heard as a cord that has thickened and that they hold at their end.
images.perceptible: Taking back the dowry in 4:20–21 becomes a pull against a rope whose other end is in her hand. The covenant is not something he gave and can reclaim. It is a thing both sides grip. ḥalla/uḥilla (made lawful) is heard as a knot being untied, so the lists of forbidden and lawful in 4:23–24 read as which knots stay tied and which are loosened. In 4:33, 'what your right hands tied' makes the same knot bodily: hands clasped in a pact.

interactions.how: the covenant is the reason the handed-over wealth cannot be pulled back (kayfa taʾkhudhūnahu wa-qad … akhadhna minkum)
4:21 puts the two side by side: the bodily arrival (afḍā) and the tied cord (mīthāq). Marriage is both.
shiqāq in 4:35 is the strain on this cord; tawfīq is the retying

images.movement: This image gives the window its spine. What was tied cannot be taken back by force, and lawfulness is measured in knots tied and untied.

images.name: Reaching into a shared space
images.source: chain map: 4. Covenant Gives Intimacy Its Form / Subchannel B. The Relation as Access and Joining
images.scene: Two people cross an open space and reach each other. They enter inside and alight in one dwelling, mixing their lives. One of them tries to put someone else in the other's place. At the end, God brings the faithful into an honoured entrance.

members.role: reaching the end point, arriving at the other
one part reaching the other part
intermingling, shared life (the ʿashīr is the spouse)
the counterpart joined to its pair
the place in the shared space that one would refill
those who alight in one dwelling (ḥalīl / ḥalīla)

images.containment: 'Some of you went in to others', and afḍā also names crossing an open space until you reach someone, so the intimacy is heard as an arrival.
images.perceptible: The marriage bond becomes spatial. afḍā is crossing open ground to the end point. dakhala is going inside. ḥalāʾil are wives, literally 'those who alight with' your sons. muʿāshara is mixing one's days with another's. So istibdāl zawj makāna zawj (4:20), 'replacing one spouse in the place of another', is the attempt to refill a place someone has already arrived at. The window's last entry, mudkhal karīm (4:31), turns this entering toward God's honoured dwelling.

interactions.how: arrival and knot stand together in 4:21
entering is lawful only through the enclosure's gate; the forbidden rings mark where one may not enter
the shared bed (maḍājiʿ) is the inmost space of this dwelling, where the cutting-off of 4:34 takes place

images.movement: This image shows what has already happened between the spouses and cannot be undone by taking back property. At 4:31 it widens into the entrance God grants.

images.name: Rings of enclosure: the forbidden circle, the fortress, and water poured outside
images.source: chain map: 5. Sexual Access Enclosed and Compensated / Subchannel A. Enclosure Against Uncontracted Spill; chain map: S12. Raised Plaster Makes a Fortress, Not an Escape from Death (ح ص ن only)
images.scene: Around a house lies a protected precinct: the kin one may never marry, and the lap where stepdaughters are raised. Past it stand the fortresses of married women. Beyond them is open ground where one may seek, but only as someone who builds a fortress, not as someone who pours water out on the ground or keeps secret companions. A false enclosure also appears: a grip that jams the exit so the woman cannot get out. Inside the true fortress, the wife guards what is hidden while the husband is away, because God guards.

members.role: false enclosure: constriction that keeps her from her right
the blocked exit, like an obstructed birth
nikāḥ al-maqt: the old name for breaching the inner ring by marrying the father's wife
the protected precinct (ḥarīm) around a dwelling
the lap or embrace where the child is sheltered
married women, walled in by a bond
the fortress whose interior cannot be reached
pouring liquid out onto the ground
being taken inside the walls through marriage
guarding what is sacred and the pledge
the husband's absence, and what is kept during it
God as the outer guard of the fortress

images.containment: Seek wives with your wealth as muḥṣinīn, men who protect by marriage, and the word also lets them be heard as builders of a fortress rather than men who pour water out on the ground.
images.perceptible: The prohibitions of 4:22–24 become a map of concentric zones. First a protected precinct of kin, including a lap. Then walled-in married women. Then 'what is beyond that', where one may go out seeking. The difference between marriage and fornication becomes material: water kept inside walls versus water poured out onto the ground to be lost. ʿaḍl in 4:19 shows the bad counterpart of the fortress, a grip that jams the exit. 4:34 reaches the fortress interior: a wife who guards in the husband's absence, with God guarding.

interactions.how: the rings decide where entering is lawful
the inner ring is drawn from the body of kinship: womb, breast, lap, loins
the walls are paid for (bi-amwālikum, ujūr); wealth builds the fortress

images.movement: This image carries the window from the abuse of women's persons in 4:19 through the protected order of 4:22–25 to the trust kept in the household in 4:34.

images.name: Given into her hand: wealth that cannot be pulled back
images.source: chain map: 5. Sexual Access Enclosed and Compensated / Subchannel B. Recognized Transfer Rather Than Seizure; chain map: S29. Set Work Generates an Owed Wage; chain map: S23. Fire Assays Gold While Gilding Imitates It (ذ ه ب only)
images.scene: Wealth, even a heap of gold, passes into a woman's hand. The man wants to walk off with part of it, or to swap her for another woman and take it back. The taker is left stunned by his own false claim. Against this stand a fixed, marked due and a mutual consent that can change it.

members.role: taking possession without contract or cost
forcing someone into what they loathe
a gold glint, heard alongside the qinṭār of the next ayah
one thing standing in another's place
a heap of gold or silver
a lie that leaves the hearer dumbfounded (plain sense)
the notch cut to mark the measure
mutual consent that may adjust the due
the due also owed to a slave woman
the recognised good manner of paying

images.containment: Take nothing back of what you gave her, even a heap of gold; farīḍa is the fixed due, and the word also keeps the notch cut to mark a measure.
images.perceptible: The ayat trace the hand's motion: given (ātā), then reached back for (akhadha), then carried off (dhahaba bi-). A qinṭār is a heap of gold, so 'not a thing' is set against a huge amount. buhtān includes the stunned state (bahata), so the man who claims the dowry back is left speechless before a claim that cannot stand. farīḍa lets the reader see the due as a marked notch, a measure cut into the record, which only both parties' consent can move.

interactions.how: the covenant is why the transfer cannot be reversed
the same pattern widens in 4:29: wealth taken without consent is 'eaten'; tarāḍī (mutual consent) links 4:24 and 4:29
payment builds the walls of iḥṣān

images.movement: This image carries the window's first complaint, women treated as property and stripped of it, into a rule of fixed, consented dues.

images.name: Eating wealth feeds the fire that eats the eater
images.source: chain map: 7. Illicit Exchange Turns Back on the Taker / Subchannel A. Exchange With or Without a Valid Basis; Subchannel B. Appropriation as Self-Killing and Fire
images.scene: Wealth lies in the space between people. It can move through consented trade, or it can be devoured with nothing true behind the claim. Devouring is a way of feeding a fire. Those who overstep and wrong others are themselves put into the fire, and what they destroy turns out to be their own selves.

members.role: feeding a fire, the fire's eating
the space between you where wealth moves
something with no truth or firm footing
blood gone to waste, with no requital
your own selves, one another as one self
putting a thing where it does not belong
meeting the fire and its heat

images.containment: Do not devour one another's wealth falsely; the verb akala also covers fire consuming its fuel, and the one who does it is himself set in fire.
images.perceptible: The prohibition becomes causal and bodily. The same akala that names consuming wealth names fire consuming wood. So 4:29–30 close a loop: whoever feeds on others' wealth is feeding a fire, and in the end becomes its fuel (nuṣlīhi nāran). 'Do not kill your selves' then reads as the other end of the same act. Wealth taken 'between you' is taken from the one self the community shares. bāṭil also names blood spilt for nothing, which makes the self-killing concrete.

interactions.how: the dowry case (4:20) is one instance of this general eating; tarāḍī links them
the answer to devouring is the allotted portion earned and asked of God (4:32)
ʿudwān is overstepping the line, the same excess as the great swerve of 4:27

images.movement: This image is the hinge where the window moves from marriage law to the whole community's wealth. It shows how grabbing turns into self-destruction.

images.name: The trodden road, the pull to the side, and the one who stands upright
images.source: chain map: 6. Directional Disturbance and Household Repair / Subchannel A. Tilt Against Responsible Standing
images.scene: A road has been trodden by those who went before. God guides the traveller along it. Others walk behind their appetites and want the traveller to swerve far off the road. To lean to one side is junāḥ; keeping to the side of what is forbidden is ijtināb. In the household, one person stands upright over the other to keep it straight, and is told not to go looking for a path against her.

members.role: the beaten roads and ways of those before

images.containment: Those who follow their appetites want you to swerve a great swerve, and the verb mayl is literally a body veering to the side of the road that God's guidance keeps you on.
images.perceptible: 4:26–28 become a road scene with a direction and a pull. God shows the trodden ways (sunan). Appetite's followers walk behind and want the traveller to veer far off. junāḥ, repeated as 'no blame on you', keeps its physical sense of leaning to a side, so each permission says: this does not tilt you off the road. In 4:34 qawwām is heard beside istiqāma (standing level), and the man's authority is bounded by the same road image: 'seek no path against them'.

interactions.how: the road is made passable for a weak walker: God lightens
nushūz (rising up) and shiqāq (splitting to two sides, including 'veering from the aim to either side') are household forms of the swerve
ʿudwān is the same overstepping

images.movement: This image gives 4:26–28 and 4:34 one orientation. God's will guides straight; appetite pulls sideways; the guardian's role is to keep upright, not to take a path against the other.

images.name: A load lightened for a body created weak
images.source: chain map: S2. Obligation Scaled to Human Capacity
images.scene: A person does not have the length of reach or the means to carry something. He fears a hardship like a steep climb, or like a bone that has been set and could break again. He is told to hold himself back patiently. God turns toward him and brings him back to lightness, easing the load, because man was created weak.

members.role: a fracture set, healing crooked (a minor echo, carried by ʿanat)
God bringing people back to lightening and permission

images.containment: Man was created weak, so God wills to lighten your burden; ʿanat, the hardship feared, is also the word for a set bone breaking again.
images.perceptible: The concession in 4:25 is given a body. ʿanat is not a vague difficulty. It is a steep climb, or a healed bone snapping again, and a weak body cannot risk either. tawba in 4:26–27 carries a classical gloss, 'He brought you back to lightening and made permissible what was barred', so God's turning is a turning toward ease. 4:28 then says it outright: yukhaffif (lighten a load) because ḍaʿīf. The run of 'God wills' (yurīdu) becomes a hand taking weight off a frail carrier.

interactions.how: the lightened load lets the weak walker keep the road against the great swerve
the slave woman's due (ujūr) is still owed; lightening does not cancel her right

images.movement: This image states the purpose behind the whole legal section: the rules are measured to a created weakness, not imposed as dead weight.

images.name: The rising, the split, and the fitting
images.source: chain map: 6. Directional Disturbance and Household Repair / Subchannel B. From Raised Resistance to Matched Mediation; chain map: S7. The Bow Is Tested, Nocked, and Drawn (و ف ق B006 only)
images.scene: Ground rises up and juts out. In the shared bed, one sleeper turns away from the other. What lay between the two, the link joining them, splits into two halves, each on its own side. Each family sends one arbiter. If they both want repair, God fits the two back together, the way an arrow's notch is seated on the bowstring. Above it all, God is the One truly high and great.

members.role: marital estrangement (plain sense; the dictionary notes it can come from either spouse)
a reminder that softens the heart
a blow (plain sense of the third step)
the true height, against every rising up
each on his own half, his own side
a group split by discord (plain sense)
the link that stands between them
the arbiter given authority to decide
his people, the side he belongs to
two things made to fit together
seating the arrow's notch on the bowstring
knowing what is inside the matter

images.containment: If you fear a breach between them, send arbiters, and God will bring them into accord; tawfīq is also the word for seating an arrow's notch on its string.
images.perceptible: The quarrel gets shape and direction. nushūz is ground rising and jutting. shiqāq is one thing cracking into two halves, each going to its side (shiqq). bayn is the joining link itself, and it is what cracks. The remedy mirrors the split: one arbiter from each half. Then God's tawfīq makes two things fit, like a notch meeting a string. It is God who fits them, and only if the two want repair. Ending 4:34 on 'God is High, Great' answers any rising-up in the household, from either spouse, with God's own height.

interactions.how: rising up and splitting to two sides are household forms of the swerve; the qawwām keeps upright but must not seek a path against her
the split is strain on the tied cord; tawfīq is its retying
the shared bed is the inmost space of the dwelling the spouses reached together

images.movement: This image closes the window. The bond tied in 4:21 is threatened and repaired. Repair is done by both families and completed by God, who knows what is inside.

images.name: The body of kinship: womb, breast, lap, loins
images.source: chain map: S11. Milk Flow Produces a Kinship Relation
images.scene: Mothers who bore you and mothers who nursed you. Milk sucked from the breast, making nursing-siblings. Stepdaughters raised in the lap. Sons from your loins. Parents and near kin leave inheritances. God's closing name, raḥīm, shares its letters with raḥim, the womb.

members.role: the mother who bears and raises
the origin that gathers and to which things return
the nursing tie that stands in for blood
the lap where the child is held
silf: the in-law tie formed when two sisters marry (minor echo right after 'two sisters')
the womb heard inside God's name after a list of womb-kin

images.containment: The list of forbidden women is drawn from the body: the mother who bore you, the breast that nursed you, the lap that raised your stepdaughter, and the loins of your sons.
images.perceptible: The prohibitions of 4:23 stop being a bare list and become a map of the body's ties: womb, breast, lap, loins. Nursing (raḍāʿa) visibly makes kin, because the dictionary defines it as a tie that stands in for blood. The ayah ends with raḥīm, sharing the root of raḥim (womb). The mercy that forgives 'what has passed' is heard in the same root as the womb these ties come from.

interactions.how: the body of kinship draws the innermost forbidden ring
in 4:33 the same kin (parents, near relatives) become heirs of allotted shares

images.movement: This image grounds the marriage law in bodies and nurture, and ties God's mercy to the womb that makes kinship.

images.name: Allotted portions and the surplus above them
images.scene: Portions are set up, each marked for its owner. Men and women each gain their own. Beyond the portions lies a surplus (faḍl) that God has given some over others. One should not picture another's portion with longing, but ask God from His surplus. What the dead leave passes to appointed heirs. Wealth is spent out, and God is present and witnessing over all of it.

members.role: the measured decree behind the portion
a fixed portion set up for its owner
the portion owed to allies bound by oath
the half as a measured share

images.containment: Do not covet what God has favoured some with over others; faḍl is also a surplus beyond the measured portion, and that surplus is to be asked of God, not taken from a neighbour.
images.perceptible: 4:32 separates two layers. There is the naṣīb, a portion set up and marked for its owner, which each person earns. Above it is faḍl, a surplus that lies outside anyone's portion and is God's to give. Coveting (tamannī) is picturing another's portion as one's own. The cure is to redirect the wanting upward: 'ask God from His faḍl'. 4:34 reuses faḍḍala together with spending (anfaqū), so precedence is tied to wealth going out, not coming in.

interactions.how: allotted, earned portions are the answer to devouring each other's wealth
the heirs of 4:33 are the kin of the body
the qawwām's precedence rests on spending and is bounded by 'seek no path against them'

images.movement: This image turns the window from forbidding (do not take, do not eat) to ordering: every person has a set portion, and the surplus is God's.

concepts.concept: Loosening what was bound: to become lawful is for a knot to be untied, and spouses are those who alight in one place once the knot of marriage allows it
An enclosure guarding an interior: a fortress, a woman's chastity, and the bond of marriage are one protected inside
Open space crossed to its end: reaching someone, and marital intimacy as that arrival
The between: both the link joining two parties and the gap separating them. Discord splits it; reconciliation restores it
Liquid poured out and lost on open ground: fornication named as seed spilled outside any vessel of contract
A tight blockage that keeps something from coming out: a woman barred from her right, like an obstructed birth
Consuming: eating food, using up wealth, and fire devouring its fuel
Leaning toward one side: bodily inclination and inclination toward sin, negated in 'no junāḥ on you'
Standing upright over something to keep it level and in one's care
One thing cracked into two halves, each moving to its own side
Two parts made to fit one another, like an arrow's notch seated on the bowstring
Thickening: a thin thing grown thick, and an oath made stringent

movement: The window opens by forbidding men to take women by force: taking them as inheritance, jamming their way out (ʿaḍl), reaching back for the gold already handed over. Against taking, it sets two things that cannot be undone: an arrival (afḍā, crossing to the other) and a cord both sides hold (mīthāq ghalīẓ). It then draws the rings of enclosure from the body of kinship (womb, breast, lap, loins) out to married women's fortresses and to the open ground beyond, where one may seek only as a fortress-builder, not as someone pouring water on the ground. At its centre, God's will is a guide on a trodden road and a hand lightening the load of a weak creature, against appetite's pull to swerve. The law then widens: devouring wealth feeds the fire that consumes the eater, while earned portions and God's surplus give each person a place. It ends in the household: a rising-up, a bond cracking in two, one arbiter from each side, and God fitting the two back together like a notch on a string. Throughout, taking and tearing are answered by binding, enclosing, allotting and fitting.

plan.note: Show hands closing on a woman: inherited like goods, the exit jammed (ʿaḍl, also an obstructed birth), part of what was handed over carried off. Against this, muʿāshara as mixing one's days with hers.
A heap of gold (qinṭār) against 'not a thing'. 'A spouse in place of a spouse' refills a place already occupied. buhtān leaves the claimant stunned.
Two irreversible facts side by side: an arrival across open space (afḍā) and a cord grown thick that the women hold at their end. This is why the dowry cannot be pulled back.
The first forbidden ring: the father's wife. maqt is also the pre-Islamic name of exactly this marriage (nikāḥ al-maqt), and 'an evil road' starts the road image.
The forbidden circle drawn from the body: womb, breast, lap, loins. ḥalāʾil are those who alight together. 'No junāḥ' keeps its sense of leaning to a side, and raḥīm echoes raḥim, the womb.

Past the walled-in married women lies 'what is beyond'. It is loosened (uḥilla) for a seeker who builds a fortress, not one who pours water out. The due is a marked notch (farīḍa) that only mutual consent can move.

For one without the reach (ṭawl), the concession is sized to a feared ʿanat: a steep climb or a set bone breaking again. The slave woman is still owed her due bil-maʿrūf, and walled in, not a secret companion.
God shows the trodden ways of those who went ahead, and His turning (tawba) is glossed as bringing people back to lightening and permission.
Two wills pull in two directions: God turning toward you, appetite's followers walking behind and wanting you to veer far to the side.
The load is taken off a frame created weak: yukhaffif because ḍaʿīf.
Wealth in the space between you. akala is also fire eating wood. Consented trade versus a baseless claim. Taking from one another is killing the one shared self.
The loop closes: the one who oversteps and devours is himself set in the fire, and that is easy for God.
Keeping to the side of the great sins has God cover the lesser ones. The window's entering motif ends in a noble entrance (mudkhal karīm).
A marked portion for each, men and women, earned. Above it lies God's surplus, to be asked for, not pictured with envy in another's hand.
What parents and near kin leave goes to appointed heirs. 'Those your right hands tied' makes the covenant knot a hand-clasp, and God is present over every portion.

The qawwām stands upright to keep level, not to seek a path against her. Inside the fortress the wife guards in his absence, as God guards. nushūz is a rising-up, met by steps that end at the shared bed, and answered by God the High, the Great.
The link between them cracks into two halves. One arbiter comes from each half. If both want repair, God fits them together like a notch on a string, and He knows the inside of the matter.

chains_set_aside.title: S6. Marked Arrows Divide the Slaughtered Camel
chains_set_aside.why: None of its members is active in this window except a distant ن ف س B016 (the fifth maysir arrow), which nothing at 4:29 calls up. The portion idea is carried by I10 through ن ص ب instead.

chains_set_aside.title: S7. The Bow Is Tested, Nocked, and Drawn
chains_set_aside.why: Only و ف ق B006 (seating the notch) earns a place, inside I8. ب ي ن B008, ع ن ت B006 and the rest have nothing to show in this window.

chains_set_aside.title: S8. A Timed Watering Turn Makes Room for the Thirsty Animal
chains_set_aside.why: س ل ف B004 and د خ ل B007 are unsupported here; the illā mā qad salaf and dakhaltum lines are better served by I9 (silf of sisters) and I2 (entering).

chains_set_aside.title: S10. Prepared Drink Moves from Mixture to Lost Sobriety
chains_set_aside.why: ق ت ل B007 (diluting wine) at 4:29 has no partner in the window and would distract from the fire loop of I5.

chains_set_aside.title: S12. Raised Plaster Makes a Fortress, Not an Escape from Death
chains_set_aside.why: Only ح ص ن B001 is present in this window, and it is absorbed into I3. The plaster, towers and death belong to 4:78.

chains_set_aside.title: S14. The Final Breath Is Enclosed in a Grave-House
chains_set_aside.why: غ ي ب B009 (the grave) is not activated at 4:34, where the wife's guarding of the absent husband's affairs (B005) rules.

chains_set_aside.title: S17. A Debt Follows Claim, Surety, Payment, and Discharge
chains_set_aside.why: Only a weak ت ب ع B005 at 4:27 touches this window. Following appetites there is a walking-behind, carried by I6.

chains_set_aside.title: S23. Fire Assays Gold While Gilding Imitates It
chains_set_aside.why: Only ذ ه ب B001 is kept, as a minor gold glint in I4 beside the qinṭār. Assaying and gilding have no members here.

chains_set_aside.title: S25. A Pot on Three Stones Is Brought to Doneness
chains_set_aside.why: ج ع ل B007 (pot-lifting cloth) at 4:19 is not activated by anything in the window.

chains_set_aside.title: S28. A Forward Sale Begins with Appraisal and Known Price
chains_set_aside.why: س ل ف B005 (advance payment) and ق و م B010 (valuation) are not activated. illā mā qad salaf is about the past, and qawwāmūn about standing and care (I6).

other_activations: 4:19:8 و ر ث B005 (stirring embers so they flame): heard faintly against the fire of 4:30; too far to join I5.
4:19:20 / 4:22:14 / 4:25:39 ف ح ش B002 (overstepping the measure): activated by ʿudwān (4:30) and the great swerve (4:27); fāḥisha as going past a limit.
4:19:26 ع س ي B006 (hoping milk will return): عسى beside 'much good' (khayran kathīran) lets the hope be heard as waiting for milk to flow again.
4:20:9 ق ن ط ر B001 (bridge): the same word as the heap of gold; nothing in the window activates it.
4:22:11 / 4:23:49 س ل ف B001 (going before, precedence): the plain 'what has passed', echoed by 'those before you' (4:26:9).
4:23:5 ء خ و B002 (tether ring; ḥurma and dhimma): the sisters' word carries the sense of a tie that is held sacred, activated by ḥurrimat and mīthāq.
4:23:20 ر ب ب B011 (rabāba, covenant): the stepdaughter word keeps a sense of covenant, activated by mīthāq (4:21) and ʿaqadat (4:33).
4:23:53 غ ف ر B001 and 4:31:7 ك ف ر B001/B009 (covering, and wiping out sin by covering it): God covering sins, a pair across 4:23–31.
4:24:28 ف ر ض B001 (the notch cut): kept inside I4 as the mark of the measure.
4:29:17 ق ت ل B007 (diluting drink to break its strength): not activated.
4:34:16 ق ن ت B002 (long standing in prayer): stands beside qawwāmūn as a second upright posture, the wives' standing before God.

4:34:29 ض ر ب B004 / B006 (holding back from something; laying a cover or barrier): attested senses heard after hajr in the shared bed. The commentary may name them as attested, but must keep the plain sense and not replace it.
4:25:15 ف ت ي B001 (youth, freshness): fatayāt keeps youth alongside its sense of a servant woman (B002).
